newsitem.title: CANADA: Gdansk grain terminal project may begin mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Gdansk grain terminal project may begin mid-1997.

text.p: Construction of a grain terminal at Poland's port of Gdansk should begin by mid-1997, said an executive for the Saskatchewan Wheat Pool, a partner in the project.

"There's some financing that has to be put together yet for some of the other partners. If all goes well I would think we'll get a start by mid-summer with about a 24 month construction period thereafter," SWP grain group general manager Bruce Johnson said.
SWP, Nova Scotia consulting firm Dessaport Corp Intenational and Pennsylvania construction firm Joseph D. Andrea are partners in the EuroPort Inc joint venture.
SWP will invest US$8.0 million for 10 percent of the joint venture with an option to buy five percent more. It will provide construction expertise and then manage the terminal.

EuroPort holds a long-term lease on 56 hectares (140 acres) of waterfront property and three berths at Gdansk's north port deep water pier. It also has exclusive rights to develop facilities to handle bulk grain, fertilizer, malt production and milling.
